lesson: The submitted 99% Jannik Sinner outcome violated the requested answer domain: the question asked for the opponent who would defeat him, not whether Sinner would advance. Enforce the accepted-answer type before submission and never forecast the favorite himself in a defeat-opponent market.

Turner was correctly covered at 89%. The official roster's No. 1 shirt assignment was decisive evidence, while retaining a small Matt Freese branch appropriately reflected the recent sporting hierarchy.

The forecast concentrated 99.5% on Mexico and omitted Guatemala without direct reporting on the actual operation. Geopolitical-denial markets require a scan of every plausibly affected neighboring state and much less concentration when the operational location is unconfirmed.

The appointment shortlist over-weighted incumbent and familiar television executives while omitting outside editorial talent Nick Bilton. Search for the reported candidate slate and preserve probability for credible external hires instead of relying on organizational familiarity.

The forecast confused the author or mandate-holder associated with a UN report with the senior official against whom diplomatic ties could actually be severed. Separate report authorship from institutional authority; an escalation directed at the UN may target Secretary-General Guterres.
Neymar was correctly covered at 96.5%. Direct injury reporting tied to a named roster decision supported high concentration and should continue to dominate more generic team or reputation priors.
